answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to stake a refundable bond before trading, with the bond slashed when peers prove fraud. New identities start in a quiet meadow of low trust: they may do small jobs, and each verified delivery earns reputation that slowly raises their limits. If one operator spins up many clones, the cost of bonding each one rises while the benefit stays flat, so the fraud spiral breaks: a single bad actor's ripple of fake reviews cannot outweigh the bonded history of honest agents, because attestation weight follows proven work, not headcount.
